object_description: long hall-like structure of pavilions beneath a folded roof
design_condition: The long elevated structure runs along the street and groups three pavilions under one roof, but its broad footprint cuts into the landscape, fails to preserve the meadow, and weakens indoor-outdoor integration.

positive.statement: The pavilion architecture has a pleasant airiness in the park.
The folded roof landscape offers a carefully developed way to complement the existing system.
The internal division creates spatial order and clarity.
Accessibility is logically provided in both longitudinal and transverse directions.
The wooden construction has comparatively low embodied energy.

negative.statement: The floating floor plate blurs the desirable interweaving of indoor and outdoor space.
The building’s surface extent gives no emphasis to settlement and open space.
The large footprint cannot meet tree-protection requirements, and the meadow is not preserved.
Raising the base plate prevents direct accessibility and requires ramps and stairs.
The close-meshed beam grid appears over-orchestrated beside the calm existing buildings.
The excessive plan depth is disadvantageous for use despite the skylights.
The room-program arrangement is not very convincing from the user’s perspective.
The auditorium has an unfavorable geometry, a stage on the long side and a foyer that is too small.
The flexible organization of the daily structures raises questions about usability, acoustics and accessibility.
The single-storey pavilion construction has higher construction and operating energy than more compact volumes.
